name: avatar
title: Avatar
description: A person or entity shown as a photo, or as initials on a soft tint when there is no photo. Also an empty seat: "+" to add someone, "?" for someone not added yet.

examples.name: avatar-demo
examples.title: Avatar
examples.description: A photo, serif initials in their name-hashed tints, a square avatar, and a broken image falling back to initials.

examples.name: avatar-group
examples.title: Group
examples.description: Overlapping avatars with a +N overflow tile.

examples.name: avatar-placeholder
examples.title: Placeholders
examples.description: A family row: four members, a "?" for one not added yet, and a "+" to add someone.

examples.name: avatar-sizes
examples.title: Sizes and decorative use
examples.description: sm, md, lg and square; alt="" next to a visible name.

examples.name: avatar-tints
examples.title: Tints
examples.description: Every fixed tint plus none. Each is a contrast-checked token pair.

props.name: name
props.description: Used for initials, the tint and the accessible name.

props.name: src
props.description: Image URL. Initials show while it loads and if it fails.

props.name: alt
props.description: Accessible name; defaults to name. Pass "" when the name is already visible next to the avatar.

props.name: shape
props.description: square follows the brand's button radius (capped at 30%).

props.name: tint
props.description: Initials colour. auto hashes name (case- and space-insensitive) into brand, accent, info, warning or success, so a person keeps their colour everywhere; danger is never auto-picked. none is an untinted neutral. Every option is a background/foreground pair the theme engine contrast-checks.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: An empty seat: a dashed circle with "+" (add) or "?" (unknown, e.g. not added yet) in text.subtle. Ignores src and tint; still named by alt ?? name.

props.name: children
props.description: Replaces the initials (or the placeholder's + / ?), e.g. an icon for a team or bot.

props.name: max
props.description: Show at most this many avatars, then a "+N" tile.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of every avatar in the group.

props.name: shape
props.description: Shape of every avatar in the group.

notes: Avatar is role="img" named by `alt ?? name`; the inner has alt="" so the name is read once.
alt="" makes it decorative (aria-hidden) — use it when the name is printed beside it.
AvatarGroup is role="group"; give it an aria-label that says who the people are.

Initials are grapheme-safe (accents, emoji, vowel signs, conjuncts) and use a zero-width non-joiner for joining scripts such as Arabic, so two letters never fuse. In Brahmic scripts the initial is the base letter, marks dropped — रेखा यादव gives रय, not रे, which at this size reads as ₹ (ADR-032).
The "+N" count is formatted and direction-isolated in the current locale.
The ring (a hairline inner edge and top sheen) is decoration; the name carries the meaning.

Initials use the heading face (serif in editorial brands) and each tint is a pair from packages/theme-engine/src/contrast-pairs.json: action.secondary.fg/bg, accent.text/accent.subtle, feedback.{info,success,warning,danger}.fg/bg, text.default/surface.sunken; placeholders use text.subtle on surface.default. text.brand on surface.selected is deliberately not used: the engine doesn't check it.
A placeholder carries no meaning by its dashes alone. Name it ("Father, not added yet") or, for "add", put it inside a Button with a label.
Avatars pop in on mount (scale 0.8 to 1 on the spring), staggered in a group; with reduced motion they simply appear.

do: Pass the full name even when you have a photo; it is the fallback and the accessible name.
Use square avatars for organisations and teams, circles for people.
Leave tint on auto for people, so the same person is the same colour in every list.
Use placeholder="unknown" for a known slot that's empty (a family member not added yet), and placeholder="add" inside the button that adds one.
dont: Don't make an avatar a button by itself; wrap it in a Button or Link with a label.
Don't show more than about five avatars in a group.
Don't use tint to mean status; a red avatar isn't an error. Use a Badge for status.
